title: Review sidecar scratchpad — incremental change notes
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for an incremental review flow I want to try as a "sidecar" to big PRs. Keep small, reversible, and observable. Mostly notes-to-self and candidate checklist items for tiny follow-ups rather than a full rewrite.

Why sidecar approach
- Large feature PRs keep getting bogged down in bikeshedding. Try shipping a minimal change plus a sidecar PR with followups and non-blocking tidy-ups.
- Sidecar = small behavior-preserving fixes, extra tests, observability hooks, perf micro-optimizations.
- Aim: keep main review focused on correctness + API surface; push ergonomics + cleanup to sidecar.

Quick TL;DR checklist (for the sidecar PR)
- Scope: <= 200 LOC, no schema migrations, no public API changes.
- Tests: add 1–2 deterministic unit tests for any uncovered edge-case.
- E2E: smoke (local harness) for route handler with short seq length.
- Metrics: add or increment a counter on the new code path (metric name + prefix).
- Logs: structured logs with route and request_id. No PII.
- Rollout: label canary=true, add feature flag toggle (if available).
- Perf: run modified module through micro-bench harness (3 runs, median).
- Doc: inline TODOs converted to GH comments for follow-ups.

Safety and regression focus
- Backwards compatibility: assert old behavior in a regression test (explicitly compare outputs).
- KV-cache priming: make sure any added cache keys are namespace-prefixed to avoid collisions.
- Retry semantics: preserve idempotency for transient errors (observed flaky tests earlier).
- Error surface: ensure new errors map to existing error codes used by monitoring dashboards.

Refactor ideas (non-blocking, put into sidecar)
- Component split: extract validate_request() from route handler (move later, small test coverage).
- Batcher isolation: make a light adapter that wraps the batcher; allows injecting a no-op adapter for tests.
- Small utility cleanup: replace repeated regex with cached compiled pattern object in utils/validation.py.
- Move model-meta logic out of handler into model_registry.get_signature() so serving-runtime code can reuse.

Observability hooks to add (cheap wins)
- Per-route token_count gauge for every generation request (helps correlate cost spikes).
- Add sampling of kv-cache hit/miss for prefix cache. 1% sample is enough.
- Add a trace span around kernel selection that includes model_id and seq_len_bucket.

Files to scan in review (search hints)
- handlers/generation.py -> grep for TODOs and repeated if blocks.
- runtime/batcher.py -> look for windowing logic and early-exit conditions.
- infra/metrics.py -> confirm metric names and label cardinality.
- tests/test_model_cache.py -> flaky on CI, see below.

Known flaky test note
- tests/test_model_cache.py::test_prefix_eviction sometimes fails when run with full test suite on my laptop. Suspect timing + LRU eviction race. Short-term: mark with @flaky(max_runs=3) in sidecar, long-term: add deterministic time mock.

Perf experiment checklist (microbench)
1) Baseline: current main branch microbench for handler (seq=32, batch=4). Record median p50/p95 token latency.
2) Add only code change under review, rerun 5x, median.
3) If delta > 6% p95 regression, back out and investigate kernel path.

Questions to ask before approving
- Does the change touch any KMS/HSM call paths? (security signoff if yes).
- Any customer-facing schema change? (requires doc + migration plan).
- Does this alter fallback routing (hosted -> dedicated)? If so, add e2e.

Follow-ups for next sprint (post-merge)
- Move pattern-match helpers to util package and add unit coverage.
- Replace magic constants in handler with named constants + tests.
- Add bench job to CI for the hot path (weekly cadence).

Slack/PR comment stubs (quick copy-paste)
- "Thanks for the PR. Left a couple of small nit comments focused on observable signals and one test suggestion. Happy to ship the main change; I can take the refactors in a sidecar if that helps unblock."
- "Sidecar plan: I'll open a follow-up after merge with small tidyups + metrics + flaky test fix. Link: RDW-1423."

Short list of tickets to link in the sidecar
- RDW-1423 (flaky cache test)
- RDW-1487 (observability: per-route token_count)

Random notes / half-formed ideas
- Could we add a lightweight "review-sidecar" label in GH that auto-adds reviewers from a small pool? Might reduce friction.
- Maybe a bot that enforces <=200 LOC for sidecars and auto-schedules merge when CI green + 1 approval.

Action items (me)
- [ ] Triage failing cache test and draft flaky fix (deadline: next Tue).
- [ ] Draft sidecar PR branch: sidecar/rdw-1423-scratch (this week).
- [ ] Run bench harness and paste numbers into PR description.

Notes-to-self: keep sidecar semantic minimal. If anything touches model weight loading, escalate to SRE + infra.

End of scratchpad.

(If this is useful, convert to a tiny template and drop in repo as .github/sidecar_template.md)
